result: The first drop hits the glass with a soft tap, a tiny percussion against the quiet hum of an empty room. It gathers courage, swells, and begins its slow descent, carving a crooked path through the dust of forgotten conversations. I watch it trace the pane, mirroring the way memories move through us—unplanned, unavoidable, leaving faint reflections in their wake. Outside, the city breathes in gray mist, streetlights bending their halos toward the damp pavement. A squirrel pauses midway across the fence, tail twitching like a metronome marking time no one asked to keep. I wonder how many moments like this slip past unnoticed, how many tiny mercies are hidden in the ordinary rhythm of rain and rust, coffee steam and creaking floorboards. These fragments accumulate, forming the quiet architecture of a life, uncovered but deeply real. We are always reaching for the extraordinary, climbing toward milestones and horizons, while the world keeps whispering its quietest truths in the language of falling water and shifting shadows. Sometimes stillness is the only compass we need, pointing us back to the present moment, where breath meets wonder and time slows just enough to be felt. Perhaps meaning isn’t something we build, but something we learn to see. The droplet reaches the sill, gathers itself, and falls beyond sight. Somewhere below, it joins a thousand others, becoming part of the ground, the roots, the green return. I do not move. I listen, letting the ordinary hold me for a little while.
